newsitem.title: USA: Choice Hotels sets franchise plans.
newsitem.headline: Choice Hotels sets franchise plans.

text.p: Choice Hotels International Inc said Thursday it has adopted a three-year plan for its franchise operations that realigns resources, implements growth and service strategies, and heightens the company's focus on consumers.
This is part of a strategy to enhance profitability for owners of 4,164 Comfort, Quality, Econo Lodge, Sleep, Clarion, Rodeway and MainStay Suites brand hotels, the company said.
Choice previously announced a plan to divide its business through a spinoff of its real estate operations.

In a move to focus more resources on franchisees, Choice said, the new organization consolidates franchise sales and services functions under five regionally based operating groups with bottom-line responsibility. Regional offices will be in Silver Spring, Md.; Charlotte, N.C.; Indianapolis, Ind.; Denver, Colo.; and Los Angeles, Calif., the company said.
Each franchisee in the Choice system will have one, regionally based contact person who will be responsible for assessing and responding to each hotel's specialized needs.
The company said Rod Sibley, senior vice president, franchise operations, oversees these new groups.

Through its new regional structure, Choice will analyze key markets in the United States and, in conjunction with its franchisees, identify the best opportunities for new development or conversion to a Choice brand. This approach to system growth will give franchisees an early opportunity for additional development within their communities.

The company said brand management, new product development and traditional consumer marketing are being combined to create more consumer focus and drive demand for Choice brand products. Barry L. Smith, senior vice president, marketing, is responsible for the newly defined marketing function.
